prior_importants.description: The run-input class now takes every root `.json`, `.yaml`, `.lock` and `.lockb`. Disk files are read through `readPlainFile`, which throws above 1 MiB. So in any repo whose root lockfile is over 1 MiB, `testInputsIntact` returns false on every merge and no file ever counts as test.

The new node_modules and tsconfig refusals match ASCII case only. A branch path such as `src/node_moduleſ/…` or `src/tſconfig.json` escapes both. Node and tsconfck still open them on APFS as `node_modules` and `tsconfig.json`.

loadsAFile looks for static specifiers, including the new import-equals check, only in source.statements (top-level). The run-time walk only matches CallExpression nodes. An `import x = require('./evil')` inside a `namespace` block has no CallExpression in the TS AST: the `require(...)` is an ExternalModuleReference. So a config holding `namespace N { import e = require('./evil'); export const v = e }` parses cleanly and the reader still returns a plain collection, even though bundling the config pulls in and runs the branch's file. This is the shape decision 143 says is refused on either side.

findings.description: The disk side of the directory comparison throws on a symlink or submodule that the commit itself holds, while the tree side lists it fine. So testInputsIntact returns false on every merge of a repo that commits a link (or submodule) under any root dot directory (.github, .claude, .husky, .vscode...).
findings.body:
**A link the commit holds under a root dot directory costs the split on every merge**

This PR widened `VITEST_RUN_INPUT` to every dot-named root entry (`typescript.adapter.ts:238-239`), so `.github`, `.claude`, `.husky` and `.vscode` are now read whole on both sides of `testInputsIntact`. The two sides read a directory differently:

- **Tree side** (`treeRoot`): `ls-tree --full-tree -r -z` lists every entry, including `120000` links and `160000` submodules.
- **Disk side** (`diskListing`): a `Dirent` for a link is neither `isDirectory()` nor `isFile()`, so it reaches
  ```ts
  throw new Error(`${path} is not read: not a plain file named on one line`);
  ```
  An uninitialised submodule checks out as an empty directory, which lists nothing against the tree's `160000` line.

**Trigger.** The target and the branch both commit `.github/copilot-instructions.md -> ../AGENTS.md`, a common setup for repos run by AI agents.
1. `cutGateCheckout` keeps it: `refuseEscapingLinks` (`merge-gate.service.ts:1558-1594`) removes only links that point outside the checkout.
2. `diskListing` throws on it.
3. The `catch` in `testInputsIntact` (`typescript.adapter.ts:894-895`) returns `false`, so no file counts as test, on every merge.

`testFiles` reads both sides from trees and accepts the same link. Only the disk check refuses it.

**Not declared in the ADR.** ADR 0143 says a file *made* a link on disk fails the check (L50-51, L453), and it accepts the fail-closed cost for build outputs at the root (L55-57). It does not say that a link or submodule *committed* in a compared directory costs the split. At the merge base, `diskListing` did not exist and the run-input list matched no dot directory, so this is new in the PR.

**Fix direction.**
- List a link as `120000 blob <oid>`, where the oid is the hash of its `readlinkSync` target text. Git hashes a link as a blob of that text, so `hash-object --stdin` (not `--stdin-paths`, which follows the link) gives it.
- Either skip `160000` entries on the tree side, or refuse them explicitly and record the cost in the ADR.
- Add a test for a link that both sides hold.

findings.description: READ_ALIAS_KEY needs at least one character after `@`, so the most common vite alias, a bare `'@'`, is refused. A vitest config with `resolve: { alias: { '@': path.resolve(__dirname, 'src') } }` was read at the merge base and now collects nothing, though `@` names no package and no scope.
findings.body:
**A bare `'@'` alias, the most common vite alias, now costs the split**

`aliasKeys` reads an alias object only when every key matches:

```ts
const READ_ALIAS_KEY = /^@[\w.-]+$/;
```

The `+` rejects the bare key `'@'`, as in `alias: { '@': path.resolve(__dirname, './src') }` or `fileURLToPath(new URL('./src', import.meta.url))`. For that key, `aliasKeys` returns `undefined`. Then `configGlobs` returns `undefined` (L398), `vitestCollection` returns `undefined`, and `testFiles` returns `[]` (`typescript.adapter.ts:859-865`).

**This is a regression.** At the merge base, `configGlobs` never read `resolve`. A plain `vitest.config.ts` with an `'@'` alias was collected. The `path`/`node:url` imports and the call-expression values don't make the reader refuse it: an existing test (`vitest-config-utils.test.ts:276-285`) accepts the same shape with an `@src` key.

**`'@'` is safe by the code's own model.** ADR 0143 (L146-154) admits "a bare `@name` … with no `/`, which names no package". Vite redirects a specifier that equals the key or starts with the key plus `/`. So `'@'` redirects only `@` and `@/…`, and neither is a package or scope name. `aliasesAScope` would `lstat` `node_modules/@`, which no package manager creates. (The vite matching rule is pinned-version knowledge, which the code and ADR already rely on.)

The fix below admits `'@'` and changes nothing else. Also note in the `READ_ALIAS_KEY` / `VitestCollection.aliases` JSDoc and in ADR 0143 that a bare `@` is read, and add a test row for it.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/d1d51c99b7b8960782828c1b3f5e59eae8a9e93f/src/adapters/vitest-config.utils.ts#L89-L95
https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/d1d51c99b7b8960782828c1b3f5e59eae8a9e93f/src/adapters/vitest-config.utils.ts#L364-L379

findings.description: `PLAIN_KEY` rejects the trailing `[]` of an ini array key. As a result, a shared `.npmrc` containing `public-hoist-pattern[]=*eslint*` (or `only-built-dependencies[]=esbuild`, `hoist-pattern[]=…`) leaves `plainVitestCollection` undefined, and `testFiles` returns `[]` on every merge. At the merge base this was collected.
findings.body:
**An `.npmrc` array key (`key[]=`) now costs the split, which hits common pnpm setups**

```ts
const PLAIN_KEY = /^[A-Za-z0-9._@/:+-]+$/;
```

**Trigger.** The target and the branch share an `.npmrc` holding `public-hoist-pattern[]=*eslint*`, a common pnpm idiom (also `only-built-dependencies[]=esbuild`).
1. `unplainKey` takes the key `public-hoist-pattern[]`, which fails `PLAIN_KEY`.
2. So `runsAFile` and then `inputLoadsAFile` are true, and `plainVitestCollection` returns `undefined` (L495-501).
3. `testFiles` returns `[]` on every merge. The same line in an operator's `~/.npmrc` makes `testInputsIntact` false through `userConfigRunsAFile`.

At the merge base, only `RUNS_A_FILE` was tested, and this file was collected.

**Refusing the trailing `[]` adds no safety.** ADR 0143 itself says ini strips an array's trailing `[]` and that `configKey` drops it (L199, L202). So `prefix[]=/p` is still refused by `namesAConfig`, and `node-options[]=` is still refused by `RUNS_A_FILE`. The spellings the plain-key rule exists for (quotes, whitespace, `[ "prefix" ]`) stay refused. The ADR names every other fail-closed cost in a "that costs … the split" sentence, but never this one. Its "(a quote, a bracket, …)" wording at L210-213 should read "other than an array's trailing `[]`".

The tests "one naming a prefix array" and "one naming a quoted prefix array" still fail closed under the fix below. Add a row showing that a shared `.npmrc` with `public-hoist-pattern[]=…` collects.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/d1d51c99b7b8960782828c1b3f5e59eae8a9e93f/src/adapters/typescript.adapter.ts#L315-L336

refuted_findings.description: Any root name in the widened run-input class that is not lower case (Gemfile.lock, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, Pipfile.lock, Podfile.lock, Taskfile.yml, a committed .DS_Store) now throws when read, so testFiles returns [] and testInputsIntact returns false on every merge of such a repo; at the merge base these names were never read and the split worked.
refuted_findings.refutation: The mechanism holds, but ADR 0143 declares it as intended fail-closed policy. The class is every root .json/.yaml/.toml/.lock, with names folded to lower case (L40-46). An entry 'named in another case at either check' counts no file as test (L89-90). 'Names in another case at the root collect nothing', even when both sides commit them (L449-451). Failing closed there is 'the price of not having to know which tool reads which name' (L56-57). Treating miscased names as unreadable predates the PR. The PR only widened the class, which the ADR declares.

process_issues.description: Round 4 budget: only correctness (2), security (2) and guards spawned; conventions, docs, context, simplicity and maintainability skipped per §4. spec skipped: no spec source (no closing keywords or linked issues).
Guards reviewer reported the typescript.adapter.ts diff output was truncated and it did not read it past the first part, nor check the new NON_ASCII export against a dead-export guard.
Validators reported `git diff` with an absolute path or `-C` was blocked for approval; they fell back to relative-path `git diff` or `git show <base>:<path>`, verdicts unaffected.
